summary.en: A **non-defining relative clause** adds extra information about something that is already clear. It is separated by **commas** (or pauses in speech) and can be removed without changing the main idea: _My sister, **who lives in Leeds**, is a vet._ You must use **who**, **which**, **whose**, **where** or **when**, never _that_, and the pronoun cannot be omitted.
summary.es: Equivalen a las explicativas españolas entre comas: «mi hermana, que vive en Leeds, es veterinaria». En inglés no se puede usar that.

form: noun, **who / which / whose / where / when** + clause, …
Commas before and after (or before only if the clause ends the sentence)
**which** can refer to a whole clause: _He passed, **which** surprised everyone._
Quantifier + **of which / of whom**: _three colleagues, **two of whom** are new_
Preposition + **whom / which** in formal style: _the manager **to whom** I wrote_

uses.text: **Extra information** about a named person or thing: _Mr Evans, **who** teaches physics, is retiring._
**Comment on a whole sentence** with which: _She never replied, **which** annoyed me._

note.en: This use of which has no equivalent with that.
note.es: Which puede referirse a toda la frase anterior: «lo cual».

uses.text: **Places and times**: _We stayed in Seville, **where** my parents were born._ _In July, **when** it's too hot, we stay inside._
**Quantities**: _He has two sons, **both of whom** are doctors._
**Compare** defining and non-defining: _My brother who lives in Paris is a chef_ (I have more than one brother) / _My brother, who lives in Paris, is a chef_ (I have only one).

mistakes.wrong: My father, that works in a bank, is retiring.
mistakes.right: My father, who works in a bank, is retiring.

why.en: That cannot be used in a non-defining clause.
why.es: Con comas no se puede usar that.

mistakes.wrong: The tower which we visited, it was built in 1890.
mistakes.right: The tower, which we visited, was built in 1890.

why.en: Put commas around the extra information and do not repeat the subject.
why.es: No repitas el sujeto: which ya lo sustituye.

mistakes.wrong: He passed the test, what surprised everybody.
mistakes.right: He passed the test, which surprised everybody.

why.en: Use which, not what, to comment on a whole clause.

mistakes.wrong: She has two brothers, who one lives in Canada.
mistakes.right: She has two brothers, one of whom lives in Canada.

why.en: With a quantity use one/two/both of whom.
why.es: «Uno de los cuales» = one of whom.

examples.en: Lisbon, which I visited last spring, is built on seven hills.
examples.es: Lisboa, que visité la primavera pasada, está construida sobre siete colinas.

examples.en: Dr Patel, whose research focuses on sleep, will give the talk.
examples.es: La doctora Patel, cuya investigación trata del sueño, dará la charla.

examples.en: The meeting was cancelled, which meant a free afternoon.
We moved to Valencia, where the cost of living is lower.
My colleagues, most of whom are under thirty, are very ambitious.
The hotel, which had just been renovated, was spotless.
In 2010, when I was still studying, I worked as a waiter.
She thanked her manager, to whom she owed her promotion.
The new phone, which costs a fortune, has a poor battery.

practice.prompt: Tom, ___ I've known for years, has just moved abroad.

explanation.en: Tom is a person and the clause is non-defining, so whom (or who) is used, not that.

practice.prompt: The train was late, ___ made me miss the interview.

explanation.en: Which refers to the whole situation of the train being late.

practice.prompt: She has three cars, two of ___ are electric.

explanation.en: After a quantity and of, a relative pronoun is needed: of which.

practice.prompt: Madrid, ___ I grew up, has changed enormously.

explanation.en: Where refers to the place and means in which.
